messages:
akshay: quick sync — ran context-mix synthetic vs replay harness this morning; saw prefill-heavy tails causing big p95/p99 regressions on the 13B q4 profile :eyes:

akshay: short summary: synthetic mix (our old seq-dist.json) underestimates prefill cost vs replay of live traces. on replay p99 latency jumps ~2.5x and CPU memcpy on host + attention kernel switching looks suspicious. raw numbers attached to the run artifacts.

maria: can you paste the exact command you used? want to reproduce locally.

akshay: sure — this is the driver 
```
./bench/replay --model redwood-13b-q4 --mix artifacts/context_mix_profile.json --qps 150 --duration 30m --seq-dist artifacts/seq_dist_longtail.json --kv-cache enabled --prefill-threshold 0.6
```

akshay: note: for synthetic we used ./bench/synthetic --mix same-file --qps 150, so same QPS but replay injects real prefill proportions and ordering which changes batching behavior.

tom: interesting — do we have flamegraphs? which kernels are hot?

akshay: flamegraphs posted in the run: attention_fused_v2 accounts for ~68% cycles on GPU for long prefill sequences, but on the replay runs we also see ~20% CPU time in kv_cache memcpy paths (host-to-device) which waits and serializes batches.

eva: that CPU memcpy is our known hotspot when batches are skewed by large prefill requests. Did kernel selection flip to a small-batch GEMM kernel for the tails?

akshay: yes — profiler shows switch: when average tokens-per-request < 256 at batch time we pick ggemm_small kernel; on long-context spikes the batch includes 1 large prefill and several tiny requests => heuristics choose wrong kernel.

maria: sounds like an apples-to-apples kernel-selection mismatch. Can we force the attention kernel to validate?

akshay: ran a forced run: 
```
./bench/replay --model redwood-13b-q4 --mix artifacts/context_mix_profile.json --force-kernel attention_fused_v2 --qps 150 --duration 10m
```

akshay: result: p99 dropped by ~28% vs the replay baseline and throughput improved, at cost of ~3% GPU occupancy loss for tiny batches.

tom: good signal — suggests heuristic should look at max-token in window or prefill indicator, not just mean tokens.

eva: agree. Proposed heuristic change: if any request in candidate batch has prefill_len > 1024 OR max_seq > 2048 then prefer attention_fused_v2, else keep existing selection. Also avoid switching kernels mid-rollout.

perf-bot: perf-regression-check: commit abc1234 reduced throughput on the replay harness by 12% on-main last night; see https://ci.redwood/perf/17589

maria: is abc1234 the kernel selector refactor?

akshay: yes — that refactor simplified selection to a single averaged metric; it lost edge-case logic for prefill dominance.

qa-bot: suggestion: add a replay-based regression test that uses live trace slice with 60% prefill proportion and validation thresholds p95/p99 within 10% of baseline.

tom: I'll add CI test under runtime-perf that runs the replay harness with the trace slice. also will add a small microbench that forces kernel choice to prevent silent regressions.

eva: can we also update synthetic generator to produce a context-mix variant that includes skewed prefill events? makes local dev reproduce easier.

akshay: created artifacts/context_mix_profile.json and pushed to s3; added instructions to bench/README.

maria: for the KV cache memcpy: is the fix to pre-stage large prefill KV on GPU earlier to avoid stall?

akshay: possible. short-term: change batching heuristics to avoid mixing a single huge prefill with many small realtime requests. mid-term: pipeline prefill KV transfer earlier and overlap with compute.

tom: action items: 1) heuristic change PR (tom) 2) CI replay regression test (tom) 3) synthetic generator update (eva) 4) KV pre-stage design doc (akshay)

maria: ETA for PRs?

tom: heuristic PR today EOD, CI test tomorrow morning.

eva: synthetic update by EOD.

akshay: I'll start the pre-stage doc draft, link in this thread when ready.

maria: thanks — this feels like a clean repro and plan. :thumbsup:
